item.title: WATCH: Savusavu residents raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall
item.description: Savusavu residents got the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he attended the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum was held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents got the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he attended the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum was held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu.

The forum, organised by the FMA , gave residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica, joined by Minister for NDRMO Mosese Bulitavu, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies were in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion was moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents shared their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities also formed part of the discussion.

The forum was livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It was held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

item.title: Year 13 students concerned as TSLS confirms no Pilot Training intake for 2027
item.description: There will be no Pilot Training intake under the Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS) 2027 cycle, a decision that has raised concerns among Year 13 students hoping to pursue careers as pilots, while Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel says the number of places is determined by demand and consultation with airlines. TSLS says the decision follows the significant number of scholarships awarded
item.content:encoded:
There will be no Pilot Training intake under the Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS) 2027 cycle, a decision that has raised concerns among Year 13 students hoping to pursue careers as pilots, while Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel says the number of places is determined by demand and consultation with airlines.

TSLS says the decision follows the significant number of scholarships awarded in recent years, with 59 students currently on active scholarships and more than 70 private students undertaking pilot training.

It says this is considered sufficient to meet Fiji Airways’ projected pilot intake requirements over the next few years.

Year 13 student of Labasa College, Shahaab Aziz, has raised concerns, saying many students in his school have been preparing for the pilot training pathway for years and are frustrated that they will not have the opportunity to apply next year.

Aziz says while students understand Government budgets can be complicated, they should at least be given the opportunity to apply and compete for available places.

Aziz says if a student applied and was not selected, they would accept the outcome, but having no intake means students do not get the opportunity to try.

He says students are also beginning to think about how decisions made by leaders will affect their future, particularly as they reach an age where they are eligible to vote.

When questioned, TSLS says the temporary pause will allow it to assess future workforce needs in collaboration with Fiji Airways and recalibrate intake levels accordingly.

It says students who wish to pursue Pilot Training in 2027 will not be provided financial assistance through TSLS and are encouraged to consider other programmes aligned with national priority areas.

Meanwhile, Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel says Government will assess the need for 2027 and could increase the number of places if there is still a need.

He says the remaining pilot training places are privately funded.

item.title: Degei acquitted of rape and sexual assault of Virgin Australia crew member
item.description: Ilaisa Tanoa Degei is now a free man after being found not guilty of raping a Virgin Australia cabin crew member. The 24-year-old was charged with one count of rape and one count of sexual assault against a 21-year-old woman.
item.content:encoded:
Ilaisa Tanoa Degei is now a free man after being found not guilty of raping a Virgin Australia cabin crew member.

The 24-year-old was charged with one count of rape and one count of sexual assault against a 21-year-old woman.

It was alleged that Degei sexually assaulted and raped the victim between 31st December 2024 and 1st January 2025 in Nadi.

W hen asked whether they will appeal the judgement, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions says it will first review the judgement before deciding.
